content.comment_body: Hello, I need some guidance about a network setup involving 10 [product_name] controllers in master mode, each with 1 [product_name] expansion module, linked to one comfort [product_name] HMI. Is it feasible to set this up? I saw on the forum that up to 31 controllers might be possible, but I’m not sure I interpreted that correctly. Was that referring to Master-Slave configuration? I can’t use Master-Slave since I require displays active on all 10 controllers. Appreciate any insights.

A comfort [product_name] panel can handle up to 8 direct connections, meaning you'll be able to link 8 controllers to the panel. For the remaining two controllers, you’ll need to relay their data through one of the initial eight. This can be achieved via a Master/Master-type connection.

Thank you for your prompt response. So just to confirm, this means I could display all 40 analog signals from all 10 controllers on one HMI? Also, is it possible to accomplish this setup on [product_name] web editor as well? Really appreciate the help.

Yes, that's possible for the HMI. As for the web server, each controller has its own. If you want to show all controllers on a single web server, you’ll need to collect data from the other nine into one central unit.
Previously, it was possible to connect one controller to eight others. Has this changed in the newer versions? If not, you'll need to use the ninth controller as a hub to reach the remaining devices.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are assessing how to connect multiple [product_name] controllers and [product_name] expansion modules to a single comfort [product_name] HMI for unified monitoring of all analog channels. A key user experience challenge is the HMI’s direct connection cap (8 devices), prompting consideration of data relaying or hub-like network architectures to enable centralized visualization while keeping display functionality on each controller.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to link all 10 [product_name] controllers to a single HMI, showing all analog points, and want to maintain active displays on every unit. They seek a simple setup for centralized data aggregation and easy monitoring.
